messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: anomalous KV-store growth + continuous-batching contention detected on pool-mistral-7b and pool-llama-70b-q8. Memory pressure crossing 92% on a subset of instances, request 5xx rate up, paging #pager. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/incidents/1799032100

alex-oncall: paging @jordan-ops and @priya-ml. I'm taking coord. alex-oncall (oncall) here; what's customer impact so far?

jordan-ops: seeing sustained tail latency and KV evictions not keeping up. KV keys count jumped 90k -> 900k in ~6m for pool-mistral-7b. A handful of workers OOM'd and restarted. Affected hosts: mistral-7b-2, mistral-7b-4, llama-70-q8-1. logs attached to incident page.

priya-ml: quick hypothesis: the recent cont-batching heuristic that merges overlapping prompts was extended to support both GQA and MQA. Somehow the canonical key formatter for llama-70b-q8 includes model-quant suffix which the GQA branch didn't strip, causing duplicate logical keys and preventing TTL/ejection to work. Also saw merge_id counters unbounded in some traces.

simon-eng: can we apply a fast fail safe? we have a route-level flag to disable cont-batch per-model: runtime.config.model[\"mistral-7b\"].continuous_batch=false. Would prefer safe-mode first rather than full rollback.

jordan-ops: applying to pool-mistral-7b canary now. command pasted: 
```
POST /api/v1/pools/pool-mistral-7b/override 
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN
{
  \"runtime.continuous_batching\": false
}
```
deploy-bot: Override accepted; rolling to 4 canary nodes -> then full pool.

alex-oncall: also reduce route max_merge_size and max_merge_time while we watch:
```
configctl set route text-gen max_merge_size=2
configctl set route text-gen max_merge_time_ms=40
```

jordan-ops: forced an ephemeral-kv sweep on canary hosts: 
```
kvctl sweep --pool pool-mistral-7b --type ephemeral --dry-run=false --removed=prefix_gqa_mqa_fix
# result: ~120k keys evicted on canary nodes
```

rachel-cs: notified customers: RetailCorp (prod), Billingly (prod), Finderly (staging). RetailCorp seeing elevated latencies on search and cart; Billingly reported degraded payment validations. CS has opened high-priority tickets.

priya-ml: I opened an emergency PR to add canonicalization guards and a merge_count cap (if merges > 3 then skip merging). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4399. Tests included for Llama quant suffix handling and GQA/MQA mixed merges. Rolling canary target.

simon-eng: canary of runtime-4399 rolled to 3 nodes; early signals show dropped KV growth on canaries and error rate falling to baseline. However we still see two legacy shards with a compat shim that was introduced in 2025-11; it stamps keys with a legacy prefix that bypasses canonicalizer.

jordan-ops: temporary mitigation for those shards: route-split 15% of prod traffic away from legacy-shim shards and into compat-backup model (lower capacity) to reduce pressure: 
```
routerctl split-route --route text-gen --model pool-mistral-7b-compat --percent 15
```

config-bot: TTL for ephemeral kv for model llama-70b-q8 was 0 (infinite) due to a config merge error on 2025-10-12. Suggest setting safe TTL 3600s as immediate fallback.

simon-eng: applying TTL emergency patch: 
```
rconf set pool pool-llama-70b-q8 kv.ephemeral_ttl=3600
rconf set pool pool-mistral-7b kv.ephemeral_ttl=3600
```

alex-oncall: handoff plan: @jordan-ops will do 45m watch and finish full pool sweep; @priya-ml will push runtime fix to main after CI and coordinate tests for merge behaviors; @simon-eng will validate config migration to prevent zero TTL on merges; @rachel-cs will coordinate customer comms and provide status to RetailCorp. I'll update incident doc and mark severity.

rachel-cs: RetailCorp confirmed partial recovery and asked for ETA on full fix. We advised rollback to cached responses for payment endpoints while ML/ops continue work. Billingly accepted route-split as mitigation and will validate.

priya-ml: after analyzing traces, root cause summary: a change to the key canonicalizer inadvertently allowed model-quant suffix variants to be treated as distinct keys when merged by cont-batch. For MQA flows we were generating merge-scoped IDs per stream without dedup, so multiple merges for the same logical prefix created unique keys and defeated eviction heuristics. Fix includes: normalize quant suffix, dedupe merge ids at canonicalization, add merge_count cap, and add metric for merge fanout.

jordan-ops: action items: 
- add KV-growth alert: if kv_key_count increases > 5x baseline in 3m -> page oncall
- add config lint to prevent kv.ephemeral_ttl == 0\/null in prod
- run global ttl sweep job to set safe TTL on all ephemeral caches
- expand CI stress test to include cont-batch + mixed GQA/MQA merge scenarios

simon-eng: filed infra follow-up tickets and assigned: INFRA-2291 (config lint), RUNTIME-1012 (canonicalizer tests), ROUTER-457 (route-split automation for degrading pools).

alex-oncall: severity: Sev2. Peak impacted requests ~22k/min across affected pools; RetailCorp & Billingly experienced ~8-13m of degraded service. No data exfiltration. Logging/metrics preserved.

priya-ml: schedule: target full rollout of runtime fix tomorrow 09:00 UTC after extended CI and canary ramp. Will add synthetic that simulates 10k concurrent merged streams to validate key stability under cont-batch.

jordan-ops: monitoring stabilized after TTL patch + cont-batch disable; memory now ~65% on previously affected hosts. closing paging loop for now; leaving elevated alerts for next 24h. ping #incidents immediately if we see a spike. :thumbsup:

simon-eng: taking follow-ups and will coordinate postmortem. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
